Mid-morning, shared rules for pickup lanes
You will learn on this page what to do first. This page covers the first checks at the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways, because a rushed start can turn into a messy handoff fast. Your job is to keep the traveler calm, keep the animal safe, and keep the record clean.

When someone arrives, greet them in a warm professional tone and look over the care plan before you promise anything. Ask yourself what the animal needs, how it handles noise, and whether the carrier or crate looks right for the species and temperament. If the traveler is anxious, slow the pace and speak clearly. The desk should feel steady, not stiff.

For small dogs, check the crate size details in the system and make sure the carrier fit is not guessed. <<FACT F068>> Then move to the rest of the booking and confirm the animal will have enough room to stay secure and settled during handling.

For large dogs, the fee rule must be checked before you move ahead with the booking. <<FACT F057>> Do not rush this part, because a missed charge creates a delay later and the traveler will be back at the counter asking for a fix.

If a traveler brings in Millie, or any other pet, treat the case the same way: verify the documents, compare the notes, and watch for anything that suggests stress, overheating, or poor fit. Use plain language, keep your tone calm, and do not promise special handling unless the care plan already supports it. If the traveler is frustrated, stay helpful and brief, then bring in the senior coordinator if the issue needs a second look.

The main thing is to match the animal, the carrier, and the booking details before the handoff moves forward. Remember to check first, speak clearly, and keep every pet plan exact.
